sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Industrials and Technology solidify their momentum leadership, while Energy sharpens its weekly decline and Healthcare's newly minted "all-green" status shows underlying fragility.

Industrials (momentum 0.867) and Technology (momentum 0.850) continue to dominate the US sector landscape. Industrials stands out as the sole sector sustaining a top-three rank across the 1, 3, and 6-month horizons, joining Healthcare (momentum 0.633) as one of only two "all-green" sectors positive across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD). Over the last five sessions, a minor rotation favored growth and select defensives, with Technology, Industrials, Healthcare, Real Estate, and Utilities each gaining 1 spot in the rankings.

In contrast, cyclical and value sectors are fading. Energy was the week's biggest loser, dropping 2 spots to rank 3rd with a momentum score of 0.433. Basic Materials, Consumer Defensive, and Financials also slipped by 1 spot each. Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the very bottom of the grid (rank 11) with a weak momentum score of 0.250, showing no signs of near-term recovery.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 2 of 11 sectors—Industrials (momentum 0.867) and Healthcare (momentum 0.633)—are positive across all weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD horizons.
* **Sustained Leadership:** Industrials is the only sector to maintain a top-3 ranking across the 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month periods.
* **Technology Dominance:** Technology holds the #1 YTD rank with a powerful momentum score of 0.850, gaining 1 spot over the last five sessions.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Energy Retreats:** Energy was the week's largest decliner, dropping 2 spots to rank 3rd, though it maintains a moderate momentum score of 0.433.
* **Broad Minor Gains:** Five sectors registered a 1-spot rank improvement over the last five sessions: Technology (to rank 1), Industrials (to rank 2), Real Estate (to rank 4), Utilities (to rank 6), and Healthcare (to rank 8). 
* **Entrenched Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.250, rank 11) and Communication Services (momentum 0.350, rank 10) failed to make any upward progress, remaining anchored at the bottom of the momentum rankings.

## Divergences
* **Fragile Healthcare Strength:** Despite achieving all-green status and rising 1 spot to rank 8, Healthcare exhibits a low agreement score of 0.39, signaling that its positive breadth is highly unstable.
* **Energy Decoupling:** Despite holding a high YTD rank of 3, Energy's near-term momentum has deteriorated to 0.433, making it the top loser over the last 5 sessions.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Technology hardware and heavy industrials maintain a firm grip on market leadership, while housing-related cyclicals surge amid a sharp weekly shakeout in uranium, retail, and capital markets.

US market breadth remains healthy with 42 of 144 industry groups holding "all-green" status across all timeframes. Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (0.995 momentum) and Electronic Components (0.980 momentum) continue to anchor the market's absolute leadership. However, a distinct rotation toward housing and consumer durables is underway, highlighted by Furnishings, Fixtures & Appliances jumping 27 spots to rank 68, and Residential Construction climbing 18 spots to rank 65. 

Conversely, defensive and commodity-linked groups are fading rapidly. Uranium plummeted 31 spots to rank 81, while Apparel Retail and Discount Stores dropped 26 and 21 spots respectively. Financial sectors are also showing signs of fatigue, with Capital Markets sliding 23 spots and Diversified Banks slipping 7 spots despite holding decent momentum. At the very bottom, Financial Data & Stock Exchanges (0.089 momentum) and Footwear & Accessories (0.100 momentum) remain deeply entrenched laggards.

## Strength
* **Tech & Industrial Dominance:** Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (0.995 momentum, YTD rank 2) and Electronic Components (0.980 momentum, YTD rank 5) lead the 42 all-green groups, showing sustained strength across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
* **Heavy Machinery & Hardware:** Farm & Heavy Construction Machinery (0.959 momentum, YTD rank 6) and Computer Hardware (0.911 momentum, YTD rank 1) remain highly resilient, maintaining top-tier momentum.
* **Service & Manufacturing Strength:** Airlines (0.85 momentum) and Textile Manufacturing (0.84 momentum) also secure all-green status, reflecting broad-based strength beyond core technology.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Furnishings, Fixtures & Appliances led the weekly advance, jumping 27 spots to rank 68 (0.73 momentum). Airlines (+22 spots to rank 39) and Real Estate - Development (+19 spots to rank 53) also posted significant gains.
* **Top Losers:** Uranium experienced the sharpest weekly decline, falling 31 spots to rank 81 (0.32 momentum). Apparel Retail (-26 spots to rank 97) and Capital Markets (-23 spots to rank 70) also fell sharply.
* **Momentum Laggards:** Financial Data & Stock Exchanges (0.089 momentum, YTD rank 134) and Footwear & Accessories (0.100 momentum, YTD rank 139) continue to anchor the bottom of the performance spectrum.

## Divergences
* **Emerging Plays:** Auto Manufacturers (+16 spots, 0.46 momentum) and Silver (+8 spots, 0.47 momentum) are showing early signs of a turnaround, jumping in rank despite still-subdued momentum scores.
* **Fading Giants:** Banks - Diversified (0.65 momentum) lost 7 spots in 5 days, while high-momentum groups like Engineering & Construction (0.79 momentum) and Communication Equipment (0.73 momentum) are beginning to slip, dropping 2 spots each.
* **Consumer & Credit Turnaround:** Credit Services and Medical Care Facilities both climbed 6 spots with identical 0.47 momentum scores, indicating a quiet accumulation in underperforming sectors.
